questions.stem: Highlight the findings that require follow-up.
questions.rationale: A systolic drop of 36 mm Hg with a rising heart rate and dizziness on standing is orthostatic hypotension, which caused a near fall. Low fluid intake and a newly started alpha-blocker are likely causes. The lack of injury and normal orientation are reassuring.

Drank about 800 mL of fluid yesterday

questions.stem: For each factor, indicate whether it contributes to the resident's orthostatic hypotension.
questions.rationale: Alpha-blockers such as doxazosin dilate blood vessels, especially after the first doses, and diuretics and ACE inhibitors lower blood pressure and volume. Low fluid intake and slower baroreceptor responses with aging add to the drop on standing. Nonskid socks help prevent falls.

rows.text: Doxazosin
Furosemide
Lisinopril
Low fluid intake
Age-related slowing of blood pressure reflexes
Wearing nonskid socks

questions.answer_summary: Doxazosin: Contributes; Furosemide: Contributes; Lisinopril: Contributes; Low fluid intake: Contributes; Age-related slowing of blood pressure reflexes: Contributes; Wearing nonskid socks: Does not contribute

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.
questions.rationale: A significant drop in blood pressure on standing with dizziness is orthostatic hypotension. Alpha-blockers can cause a marked drop in the first days of therapy, which is worse with diuretics and dehydration. There are no focal neurologic signs of a TIA.

options: the first-dose effect of doxazosin combined with diuretic use and low fluid intake
too little salt in the diet

questions.stem: Which fall prevention measures should the LPN/VN put in place? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Changing position slowly, a low bed with the call light in reach, adequate fluids, and assistance with walking reduce falls from orthostatic hypotension. Standing quickly worsens the drop, and restraints increase injury and are not a fall prevention measure.

options.text: Teach the resident to sit on the edge of the bed before standing
Keep the bed low and the call light within reach
Encourage fluids unless they are restricted
Help the resident walk until the dizziness resolves
Have the resident stand up quickly to get past the dizziness
Apply a vest restraint at night

questions.answer_summary: A, B, C, D

questions.stem: The resident's 0900 medications include lisinopril and furosemide. What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: With symptomatic orthostatic hypotension, the provider needs to decide whether to hold or adjust the blood pressure medicines, so the LPN/VN reports the readings before giving them. Giving them as scheduled risks a fall, holding everything without reporting skips the provider, and bed rest does not address the cause.
questions.answer_summary: B

options.text: Give both medications as scheduled, since the lying blood pressure is within normal limits
Report the orthostatic readings to the RN and provider before giving them
Hold all of the resident's medications for the day without telling anyone about it
Give the medications and have the resident stay in bed for the rest of the day

questions.rationale: A stable standing blood pressure without dizziness, steady walking, better fluid intake, and no falls show improvement. Nighttime dizziness when getting up to urinate is still a fall risk and needs follow-up, such as a bedside commode and reviewing the timing of doses.

rows.text: Standing BP 128/74 mm Hg with no dizziness
Walks to the dining room steadily with a walker
Drinks about 1,500 mL a day
No falls in 1 week
Dizzy when getting up at night to urinate

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.
questions.rationale: A high TSH and low free T4 with classic symptoms indicate undertreated hypothyroidism. Levothyroxine absorption is reduced by food and by calcium and iron supplements, and missed doses add to the problem. Taking it on an empty stomach with water is correct.

options: hypothyroidism that is not adequately treated

questions.stem: Which instructions about levothyroxine should the LPN/VN reinforce? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Taking levothyroxine consistently on an empty stomach and separating it from calcium and iron improves absorption, and reminders support adherence. Chest pain or palpitations can signal too much thyroid hormone, especially in older adults. Levothyroxine is usually lifelong, and calcium taken at the same time blocks absorption.

options.text: Take it every morning on an empty stomach with water, 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast
Take calcium and iron supplements at least 4 hours apart from it
Use a pill organizer or a phone alarm as a reminder
Report chest pain or a racing heartbeat
Stop taking it once you feel better
Take it with the calcium supplement to protect your bones

questions.answer_summary: A, B, C, D

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is visiting for wound care. What should the LPN/VN do about these findings?
questions.rationale: New or worsening findings outside the reason for the visit still need to be reported so the team can coordinate care with the provider. The LPN/VN does not change medication doses, and attributing the symptoms to aging or ignoring them delays treatment.
questions.answer_summary: D

options.text: Tell the client to double the levothyroxine dose for the next week to catch up on missed doses
Tell the daughter that slowing down like this is a normal part of aging at the client's age
Focus only on the wound care, since the thyroid is not part of today's visit
Report them to the RN case manager so the provider can review the thyroid treatment
